name: Technique - Gun glue and resample
description: Standalone technique from the machine-gun checklist: group the layers, glue with OTT and saturation, resample, then make filtered variations.

ingredients.source: Sub, body, click and tonal layers

manual.instruction: Group the sub, body, click and tonal layers. Balance them before adding glue so no layer is hiding a problem.
manual.verify: The layers are audible as one gesture before compression.
manual.why: MOONBOY groups the four layers and processes them together.

manual.instruction: Glue with OTT, saturation and a glue compressor. A/B against the unglued group and match perceived level.
manual.verify: The hit is denser and louder without becoming a flat wall.
manual.why: MOONBOY uses saturators, OTT and glue compression; Dripment uses a repeatable OTT/Saturator loud rack.

manual.instruction: Resample the group to audio. Keep the dry resample and make a band-passed phone-filter fill from a copy.
manual.verify: The resampled gun keeps its transient and the fill is clearly a variation.
manual.why: MOONBOY resamples the grouped bass and uses a band-pass filter for a pre-drop fill.

manual.instruction: Add a disperser or pitch-shifted copy for further variations, but leave the main gun dry and mono-compatible.
manual.verify: The variations share the same identity without smearing the drop.
manual.why: MOONBOY uses a disperser and pitch changes on resampled basses.

notes: Sources: MOONBOY, 'HOW TO TEAROUT DUBSTEP' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nApsgDWSQ7Y); Code: Pandorum, 'MACHINE GUN BASS DESIGN' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sk--QbE_TM0); Wheysted Music, 'SERUM TEAR-OUT GUN BASS TUTORIAL' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KkXF4T_WPbY); Dripment, '2 TEAROUT Serum 2 BASS ROUTINES' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NRfK34KZIf8).
